options.b: When the filling selector is turned to the Green system position
options.c: Only when the reservoir is overfilled

justification: The procedure for reservoir filling states: 'Turn the selector to the green system position. Make sure that on the quantity indicator the green light comes on.'

question: What action should be taken if the Green reservoir is overfilled during servicing?

options.a: The excess fluid must be drained to allow correct pressurization
options.b: The system must be pressurized to 77 psi to vent the excess
options.c: The PTU must be run for 5 minutes to circulate the fluid

justification: The manual warns: 'If a reservoir is overfilled, you cannot pressurize it correctly and you must drain it.'

question: Where is the manual handle for the Green system reservoir depressurization located?

options.b: On the Green ground service panel
options.c: In the aft cargo compartment

justification: The manual states: 'A manual depressurization valve is fitted on each ground service panel to depressurize each reservoir.'

question: Where is the Blue hydraulic reservoir located on the aircraft?

options.a: In the main landing gear bay
options.b: Aft of the main landing gear bay on the LH side
options.c: Inside the yellow hydraulic bay

justification: According to the component location section, the blue reservoir is located aft of the main landing gear bay on the LH side.

question: What is the normal fill level for the Blue hydraulic reservoir?

options.b: 6 liters
options.c: 12 liters

justification: The training manual specifies that the normal fill level for the blue reservoir is 6 l (1.58 US gal).

question: What is the low level warning range for the Blue hydraulic reservoir?

options.b: Between 2.0 and 2.3 liters
options.c: Between 3.0 and 3.4 liters

justification: The manual states that the blue reservoir low level warning occurs between 2.0 and 2.3 l (0.52 and 0.6 US gal).

question: What is the purpose of the 'Acoustic Filter' in the Blue hydraulic system?

options.a: To reduce the noise of the RAT during deployment
options.b: To remove the pulses of pressure from the electrical pump HP flow
options.c: To filter out microscopic metallic debris from the fluid

justification: The manual states: 'The acoustic filter is installed in the outlet from the blue electrical pump. It removes the pulses of pressure of the HP flow from the pump.'

question: What physical form does the Blue system acoustic filter take?

options.b: An empty metal sphere
options.c: A coiled high-pressure hose

justification: The manual describes the acoustic filter as 'an empty metal sphere, with inlet and outlet connections on opposite sides.'

question: How is the Blue hydraulic system typically pressurized for maintenance purposes on the ground?

options.a: By using the Yellow system hand pump
options.b: By using a ground power unit to run the blue electric pump
options.c: By manually cranking the RAT turbine

justification: The manual specifies: 'On ground it is possible to pressurize the blue hydraulic system from a ground power unit' (running the electric pump).

question: At what temperature does the Blue electric pump trigger an ECAM signal due to pump body overheating?
justification: The manual states: 'A temperature switch sends a signal to the ECAM if the pump body temperature exceeds 165°C.'

question: What is the function of the phase unbalance detector associated with the Blue electric pump?

options.a: To monitor the rotation speed of the pump
options.b: To protect the electric circuit by stopping the motor if a fault occurs
options.c: To synchronize the AC power from Bus 1 and Bus 2

justification: The manual states: 'The system has a current transformer and a phase unbalance detector which protect the electric circuit from the electric pump... It uses this signal to stop the supply of power to relay and thus stop the motor.'

question: After the phase unbalance detector has stopped the Blue electric pump, how is the unit reset?

options.a: Automatically when the fault is no longer detected
options.b: By cycling the BLUE ELEC PUMP pushbutton switch
options.c: Only by a maintenance reset on the FCDC panel

justification: The manual explains: 'When the unit has operated, it stays in that condition until it is set again. This happens automatically when the supply of power to the unit is stopped (through operation of P/BSW HYD/BLUE/ELEC PUMP) and then started again.'

question: What is the threshold for the Blue system priority valve to ensure pressure is sent to primary flight controls?

options.b: 1842 psi
options.c: 2200 psi

justification: The manual identifies the threshold of the blue priority valve as 1842 psi (127 bar).

question: Where is the Yellow hydraulic reservoir located?

options.a: In the main landing gear bay
options.b: Inside the yellow hydraulic compartment in the RH belly fairing
options.c: In the LH wing root

justification: The manual states the yellow reservoir is located inside the yellow hydraulic bay/compartment in the RH belly fairing, FWD of the MLG compartment.

question: What is the normal fill level for the Yellow hydraulic reservoir?

options.b: 12 liters
options.c: 14 liters

justification: The training manual specifies that the normal fill level for the yellow reservoir is 12 l (3.17 US gal).

question: What logic prevents flap movement when the Yellow electric pump is operated for cargo door use?

options.a: The PTU is automatically inhibited and a signal is sent to SFCC 2
options.b: The ELAC 1 computer is switched to backup mode
options.c: A mechanical lock is engaged in the Flap PCU

justification: The manual states: 'In case of cargo door operation, the PTU is inhibited, the yellow leak measurement valve is closed and a signal is sent to the Slat Flap Control Computer (SFCC) 2 to prevent flaps movement.'

question: Through which filter does the Yellow electric pump cooling and lubricating flow pass?

options.b: The return filter
options.c: The suction line strainer

justification: The manual specifies: 'The yellow electric pump cooling and lubricating flow goes through the return filter.'

question: What component is uniquely found in the Yellow system for manual ground operations?

options.b: A hand pump for cargo door operation
options.c: The Ram Air Turbine

justification: The manual identifies that 'The yellow system also has a hand pump dedicated to cargo door operation.'

question: Which signal is used as a backup in the toilet system if the SDAC cannot deliver differential pressure information?

options.b: The landing gear signal
options.c: The engine N2 speed signal

justification: According to the note in ATA 38: 'The landing gear signal is used as a back-up in case the SDAC can not deliver altitude/ diff. press information.'

question: What is the purpose of the 'leak measurement valve' when it is set to OFF on the maintenance panel?

options.a: It prevents fluid from entering the reservoir
options.b: It isolates the flight controls for testing purposes
options.c: It forces the PTU to start

justification: The manual states: 'The leak measurement valve isolates the flight controls when the guarded LEAK MEASUREMENT VALVES P/B on the maintenance panel is set to OFF.'

question: Where is the handle for the Yellow system hand pump stowed?

options.a: On the Green ground service panel
options.b: At the yellow servicing panel
options.c: In the forward cargo compartment

justification: The servicing instructions state: 'the handle is stowed at the yellow servicing panel.'

question: During Yellow system servicing, why must the electric pump be set to ON momentarily?

options.a: To check for internal leaks in the PTU
options.b: To make sure the brake accumulator is pressurized
options.c: To bleed the NWS system

justification: The reservoir filling procedure specifies: 'Set the yellow electric pump to ON to make sure that the brake accumulator is pressurized, then set the pump to OFF.'

question: What is the low level warning threshold for the Yellow hydraulic reservoir?

options.b: 3.0 liters
options.c: 6.0 liters

justification: The training manual states the yellow reservoir low level warning is 3.0 ± 0.4 l.

question: What are the primary sources of air for the hydraulic reservoir pressurization unit?

options.a: Engine 1, the pneumatic manifold (both engines/APU), and ground supply
options.b: Engine 2 only and a dedicated electric compressor
options.c: Bleed air from the HP turbine section only

justification: The manual lists the sources as Engine 1 (usual operation), the pneumatic system (both engines/APU if Eng 1 lost), and ground supply.

question: What is the regulated outlet pressure of the reservoir pressurization unit?

options.b: 50 psi
options.c: 77 psi

justification: The manual states: 'The pressure reducing valve outlet pressure is 50 psi (3.5bar).'

question: What is the purpose of the 'Restrictor' in the reservoir air supply line from Engine 1?

options.a: To increase air pressure to 77 psi
options.b: To limit airflow and reduce air temperature to a satisfactory level
options.c: To filter out engine oil mist from the bleed air

justification: The manual specifies: 'A restrictor limits the airflow and reduces the temperature of the HP air to a satisfactory level.'

question: When does the automatic drain valve in the reservoir water separator open?

options.b: After each engine or APU shutdown
options.c: When air pressure exceeds 50 psi

justification: The manual states: 'One is an automatic drain valve that is opened after each engine or APU shutdown.'

question: What ensures the pressurization system remains airtight after engine shutdown?

options.a: Manual locking handles on the service panel
options.b: Reservoir check valves downstream of the pressurization unit
options.c: A solenoid-operated shut-off valve in the bleed line

justification: Downstream of the reservoir pressurization unit, the air supply is divided into three flows to supply the reservoirs through their related check valve. These maintain pressure after shutdown.

question: What safety equipment must be worn when using the manual depressurization valve on the ground?

options.b: Eye protection
options.c: An oxygen mask

justification: The warning states: 'WHEN USING THE MANUAL DEPRESSURIZATION VALVE, PUT ON EYE PROTECTION AND KEEP AWAY FROM THE OUTLET... THE AIR CAN BE HOT AND CONTAIN PARTICLES.'

question: For how long must the pressurization system be able to maintain pressure after an engine shutdown on the ground?

options.b: 12 hours
options.c: 24 hours

justification: The manual states: 'Make sure that the pressure is kept for until 12 hours after engine shutdown on ground.'

question: How long must pressure be maintained after an air supply failure in flight?

options.b: 3 hours
options.c: Until landing

justification: The manual states: 'and for until 3 hours after a failure of the air supply in flight.'

question: What tool can be installed on the depressurization valve for long-time depressurization tasks?

options.b: A depressurization tool
options.c: A vacuum extraction hose

justification: The manual states: 'For long time depressurization, a depressurization tool can be installed on the depressurization valve.'

question: At what pressure does the bleed air system typically provide 'alternate supply' to the reservoirs?

options.b: 43 psi
options.c: 50 psi

justification: The manual specifies that reservoirs are pressurized from the bleed air system for alternate supply at 43 psi.

question: What are the two types of galley locations available in the A320 family?

options.b: Internal and external
options.c: Permanent and auxiliary

justification: The manual states: 'There are two types of galley locations, fixed and flexible.'

question: Which aircraft model has flexible galley locations in the forward emergency exit door area?
justification: Flexible galley locations in forward emergency exit door area are only for the A321.

question: How are galleys attached to the floor structure to provide flexibility?

options.a: Using permanent welds to the fuselage frames
options.b: Using seat rail attachments or hard points on longitudinal beams
options.c: Using high-strength adhesive tape and vibration isolators

justification: Galleys are mounted to the floor structure on existing seat rails or hard points which are fixed on additional longitudinal beams.

question: What degree of flexibility is provided by hard point attachments for galleys?

options.b: 2 inches by 2 inches
options.c: 6 inches by 6 inches

justification: The manual states: 'Seat rail attachments provide inch-by-inch flexibility and hard points provide 2 inches by 2 inches flexibility.'

question: What components form the upper attachment of a galley unit?

options.a: A set of three gravity locks
options.b: A bracket and two adjustable tie rods
options.c: A single oversized bolt through the ceiling frame

justification: Upper attachments consist of a bracket and two adjustable tie rods.

question: What must be done to the aircraft water system before removing a galley unit?

options.a: It must be pressurized to 50 psi
options.b: It must be drained
options.c: It must be filled with disinfectant

justification: In the removal procedure for galleys, one of the steps is to 'drain the A/C water system.'

question: Where are the potable water and waste water connections located on a wet galley unit?

options.b: On the bottom of the galley
options.c: Behind the oven module

justification: The manual states: 'the typical potable water and waste water connections which are located on the bottom of the galley.'

question: Which galley equipment requires an operational test after installation?

options.b: The coffee maker, water heater and oven
options.c: The dummy metal windows

justification: The installation procedure states: 'do an operational test of the coffee maker, water heater and oven.'

question: Where are the electrical connectors for the galley power supply usually found?

options.b: In the ceiling
options.c: On the adjacent partition wall

justification: The manual states: 'The connectors are found in the ceiling.'

question: What is the requirement for the wiring length when installing or removing a galley?

options.a: It should be as short as possible to prevent signal noise
options.b: It should contain sufficient free length to allow removal and installation
options.c: It must be exactly 1.0 meter long

justification: The manual specifies: 'The wiring should contain sufficient free length to allow removal and installation of the galley unit or galley equipment.'

question: What material is typically used for the assembly of a complete lavatory unit?

options.b: Composite material
options.c: Stainless steel

justification: The manual states: 'Each lavatory, made of composite material, is a completely assembled housing with an integrated floor.'

question: Where are flexible lavatories installed?

options.b: In assigned flexibility areas
options.c: Only in the aft-most section of the cabin

justification: The manual states: 'flexible lavatories units are installed in assigned flexibility areas.'

question: How many lower attachments are typically used for a lavatory unit?

options.b: Four
options.c: Six

justification: Lower attachments are obtained by means of four hard points or four seat rail attachments.

question: Where are the upper attachments located for lateral lavatories?

options.b: At the top and at the rear side
options.c: On the ceiling panel frame only

justification: Lateral lavatories have one attachment at the top and one attachment at the rear side.

question: Which lavatory door option is described as opening inwards and closing automatically with a damper?

options.b: Bi-folding door
options.c: Sliding pocket door

justification: The manual describes the bi-folding door option: 'A bi-folding door that opens inwards... Once opened, the door closes automatically thanks to the damper.'

question: How can a lavatory door be unlocked from the outside in case of an emergency?

options.a: By using a special EASA-certified master key
options.b: By lifting the lavatory cover-plate and pushing the unlocking pin
options.c: By rotating the handle counter-clockwise three times

justification: The manual states: 'In case of emergency, the door can be unlocked from outside without using a special tool. Lift the lavatory cover-plate and push the unlocking pin.'

question: Which two systems must be drained before the removal of a lavatory unit?

options.b: The potable water system and the toilet system
options.c: The oxygen and pneumatic systems

justification: The safety precautions for removal/installation specify: 'drain the potable water system and the toilet system.'

question: What specific caution is given regarding the use of solvents during lavatory installation?

options.a: Solvents must never be used on composite materials
options.b: Be sure that sufficient air is supplied when using solvents or sealants
options.c: Solvents must be heated to 45°C before application

justification: A warning states: 'AS SOLVENTS, SEALANTS AND OTHER SPECIAL MATERIAL ARE USED, BE SURE THAT SUFFICIENT AIR IS SUPPLIED.'

question: Which of the following is an interface for a lavatory unit according to the D/O?

options.b: Vacuum exhaust
options.c: High-pressure bleed air

justification: The manual lists 'typical vacuum exhaust' as one of the interfaces for a lavatory unit.

question: What is the requirement for the C/Bs during the installation of a lavatory unit?

options.a: They must be closed to test the lighting
options.b: They must be open, safetied and tagged
options.c: They must be removed from the panel

justification: The manual states: 'make sure that corresponding C/Bs are open, safetied and tagged' during maintenance.

question: Where is the Seat Electronic Box (SEB) located in a passenger seat assembly?

options.b: Between the front and rear legs
options.c: Behind the backrest pocket

justification: The manual states: 'The Seat Electronic Box (SEB)... is installed between the front and rear legs.'

question: What is the primary function of the Seat Electronic Box (SEB)?

options.a: To control the hydraulic recline mechanism
options.b: To serve the Passenger Service Units (PSUs)
options.c: To monitor seat belt tension

justification: The manual states: 'The Seat Electronic Box (SEB), which serves the Passenger Service Units (PSUs) is installed between the front and rear legs.'

question: How is the backrest of a standard passenger seat reclined and folded?

options.b: Hydraulically reclined and mechanically folded forward
options.c: Mechanically reclined and folded via a cable system

justification: The manual states: 'The upholstered backrest assembly of each seat can be hydraulically reclined... The backrest can be mechanically folded FWD.'

question: Which component converts 115V AC/400Hz to 110V AC/60Hz for passenger seat power outlets?

options.b: The In-Seat Power Supply (ISPSU)
options.c: The CIDS Director

justification: The manual states: 'The ISPSU converts the electrical power into 110V AC/60Hz and provides the Outlet Unit (OU).'

question: Which armrests on a multi-seat unit are not foldable?

options.b: The outer armrests
options.c: All armrests are foldable

justification: The manual specifies: 'The outer armrests of a seat unit are not foldable. The armrests between the seats can be folded up.'

question: How is a passenger seat assembly detached from the seat tracks?

options.a: By unscrewing four permanent structural bolts
options.b: By placing the quick release device in the UP position
options.c: By sliding the seat to the forward end-stop and lifting

justification: The manual states: 'By placing the quick release device in the UP position, the seat can be moved on the tracks or removed completely.'

question: During which flight phases is the electrical power supply to the PED power outlets cut off?

options.b: During take-off and landing
options.c: Only when the seat belt sign is ON

justification: The manual states: 'There is no electric power supply to the PED power outlets during take-off and landing.'

question: Which panel allows the crew to enable or disable the power for passenger portable electronic devices?

options.b: The Flight Attendant Panel (FAP)
options.c: The ELAC maintenance panel

justification: The manual states: 'The passenger PED Power P/BSW on the FAP enables or disables the portable electronic device power.'

question: Where is the reclining control pushbutton for the passenger seat backrest installed?

options.a: On the side of the headrest
options.b: In the armrest
options.c: Under the front of the seat pan

question: Where are the holders for life vests found on a passenger seat?

options.b: Below each seatpan
options.c: Inside the outer armrest

question: In the A320 potable water system, what provides a visual indication that the service panel door is open?

options.b: The text 'GROUND SERVICE DOOR OPEN' on the Flight Attendant Panel

question: Through which unit is water quantity information sent to the CIDS director for display on the FAP?

options.b: Decoder/Encoder Unit (DEU) B
options.c: SDAC 2

justification: The manual states: 'The quantity transmitter... also sends the information to a Decoder/Encoder Unit (DEU) B, which in turn interfaces with the active Cabin Intercommunication Data System (CIDS) director.'

question: What is the difference between A320 and A319/A321 filling control logic?

options.a: A320 requires two engines running to fill
options.b: A320 uses two valves for filling, while A319/A321 uses one combined valve
options.c: A319/A321 requires a dedicated air compressor during filling

justification: The manual states: 'On the A320 only, two valves are used for filling... On A319 and A321, one valve is used for filling: the overflow/fill/drain valve.'

question: In the A320 potable water system, what indicates that the overflow valve is in the open position?

options.a: The quantity gauge needle enters the red zone
options.b: The overflow valve light comes ON
options.c: A buzzer sounds in the aft galley

question: When does the 'FULL LIGHT' on the potable water service panel illuminate?

options.b: When the tank sensor triggers it and the fill/drain valve returns to closed
options.c: Only when the ground service vehicle pump is stopped

question: What is the consequence of leaving the potable water system undrained during cold weather night stops?

options.b: There is a risk of system damage due to ice formation
options.c: The air compressor will run continuously

justification: The manual warns that in winter conditions, the potable water system must be drained during night stops to prevent damage by ice.

question: During the draining of the potable water tank on an A320, where does the majority of the water exit the aircraft?

options.b: From the tank drain port
options.c: From the overflow valve

justification: The manual states: 'Most of the water will come from the tank drain and only a small amount from fill/drain and FWD drain valve.'

question: What happens to the FAP water indication page when the potable water service panel is closed?

options.b: It disappears
options.c: It switches to the waste quantity page

justification: The manual states: 'The potable water service panel is closed so the door limit switch will cut the power. The FAP water indication page disappears.'

question: If there is no electrical power on an A319/A321, how must the potable water valves be operated for draining?

options.b: They must both be manually operated
options.c: They are automatically opened by gravity

justification: A note in the manual states: 'On , A319 and A321, if there is no electrical power both valves must be manually operated.'

question: What should be done to the drain valves in cold weather conditions after the potable water system is completely drained?

options.a: They should be closed to seal the system
options.b: They should remain open to prevent damage
options.c: They must be lubricated with de-icing fluid

justification: The manual specifies: 'In cold weather conditions, the drain valves should remain open after the potable water system is drained to prevent damage.'

question: What is the primary material used for the framework of cabin attendant seats?

options.b: Aluminum
options.c: Titanium

question: Where is the life vest typically stored on a cabin attendant seat?

options.a: In a pocket on the backrest
options.b: In a compartment closed by velcro tapes in the lower part of the seat
options.c: Inside the headrest cushion

question: What mechanical feature ensures the cabin attendant seat pan returns to its stowed position when not in use?

options.b: It is spring-loaded to retract
options.c: A cable-pulley system connected to the floor

question: What type of safety harness is fitted to cabin attendant seats?

options.b: A seat belt and shoulder harness with a center buckle
options.c: A dual-inertia reel shoulder harness with six attachment points

justification: The manual describes the safety harness as having 'a seat belt and a shoulder harness with a center buckle.'

question: How is the shoulder harness on a cabin attendant seat managed when not in use?

options.a: It must be manually clipped into a side stowage bracket
options.b: It is pulled in automatically on inertia reels
options.c: It is folded into the headrest compartment

question: How are wall-mounted cabin attendant seats typically attached to the aircraft structure?

options.b: With six bolts to partitions or lavatory walls
options.c: With a single structural hinge and a safety pin

justification: The manual specifies for wall-mounted seats: 'The three sections of the wall-mounted cabin attendant seat are attached with six bolts to: partitions, lavatory walls.'

question: How are swivel attendant seats attached to the aircraft?

options.b: By hardpoints to the cabin floor structure
options.c: Directly to the door frame structure

justification: The manual states: 'Swivel attendant seats are always attached to the cabin floor structure by hardpoints.'

question: What feature of the third occupant seat headrest allows for maintenance access to the C/B panel?

options.b: It can be folded down while the seat is stowed
options.c: It slides vertically out of the way

justification: The manual states: 'The headrest can be folded down so that the C/B panel can be opened while the seat is in its stowed position.'

question: Where is the handle to lock or unlock the inertia reel on the third occupant seat located?

options.a: On the back of the seat
options.b: On the left hand side of the seat
options.c: Integrated into the buckle assembly

justification: The manual specifies that the inertia reel is 'controlled by a handle installed on the left hand side of the seat.'

question: Which occupant seat is described as non-adjustable and folding, and is optionally installed?

options.b: The fourth occupant seat
options.c: The jump seat at Door 1L

justification: The manual states: 'The fourth occupant seat is a non-adjustable folding seat... [it] is optionally installed.'

question: Which aircraft computers receive pilot orders from the side sticks and throttle position signals to calculate surface deflections?

options.b: ELevator Aileron Computers (ELAC) and Spoiler Elevator Computers (SEC)
options.c: Flight Management Guidance Computers (FMGC)

justification: The manual states that pilot orders like side stick and throttle position signals are transmitted to the ELACs and SECs, which then calculate elevator, aileron, spoiler, THS, and rudder deflection.

question: What is the primary function of the pushbuttons (P/Bs) located on the Flight Control panels (23VU & 24VU)?

options.a: To manually override the hydraulic supply to the THS
options.b: To engage, disengage, or reset their respective computer software
options.c: To toggle between Normal Law and Direct Law manually

justification: The EFCS Control Interface section states that P/Bs located on the FLighT ConTroL panels are used to engage/disengage or reset their respective computer software.

question: How does the EFCS utilize the hydraulic pressure status received from the aircraft systems?

options.a: To modulate the voltage supplied to the LVDTs
options.b: For the activation or deactivation of the related servo controls and laws
options.c: To calculate the fuel flow required for center of gravity trimming

justification: The manual states: 'The hydraulic pressure status is sent to the ELACs and SECs for activation or deactivation of the related servo controls and laws.'

question: Besides rudder control, what other system uses the signal from the rudder pedal transducers via the ELACs?

options.b: The Nose Wheel Steering system via the Braking Steering Control Unit (BSCU)
options.c: The Cabin Intercommunication Data System (CIDS)

justification: The manual states: 'The signal from the rudder pedal transducers is used for nose wheel steering via ELACs / Braking Steering Control Unit (BSCU)...'

question: When the autopilot is active, which computers receive the pitch, roll, and yaw orders from the FMGC?

options.b: The ELACs and FACs
options.c: The LGCIUs and SFCCs

justification: Under the FMGC interface description: 'If the autopilot is active, pitch, roll and yaw orders computed by the [FMGC] are sent to the ELACs and FACs, which control and monitor the surface deflections.'

question: What information is sent to the ELACs and FACs to signal that the pilot has taken control of the rudder pedals for turn coordination?

options.a: A discrete 'PEDAL DISCONNECT' signal from the sum point
options.b: The rudder pedal position signal from the transducers
options.c: A hydraulic pressure drop signal from the rudder actuators

justification: The manual states that the rudder pedal signal is used 'to tell ELACs / FACs that the pilot is now in control for turn coordination, while yaw damping signals are maintained.'

question: Which of the following is correct regarding the transmission of hydraulic pressure status to the Flight Augmentation Computers (FACs)?

options.a: FACs only receive pressure status for the Green system
options.b: FACs receive pressure status at least for Yellow and Green for the yaw damper actuator
options.c: FACs do not receive hydraulic pressure data as they are purely aerodynamic computers

justification: The EFCS Control Interface notes: 'The hydraulic pressure is also sent to the Flight Augmentation Computers (FACs), at least for yellow and green for the yaw damper actuator.'

question: During troubleshooting, if an ELAC needs to be software-reset from the cockpit, where is this performed?

options.a: On the MCDU maintenance page only
options.b: Using the pushbuttons on the Flight Control panels on the overhead console
options.c: By cycling the related ADIRU master switches

justification: The manual states that pushbuttons (P/Bs) located on the Flight Control panels (23VU & 24VU) are used to engage/disengage or reset their respective computer software.

question: According to the EFCS diagram, which computer is primarily responsible for sending 'Autopilot (Pitch, Roll and Yaw orders)' to the ELACs?

options.b: FMGC
options.c: ADIRS

justification: The system overview and interface diagrams show that the FMGC provides autopilot commands (Pitch, Roll, and Yaw) to the ELAC and FAC computers.

question: Which unit serves as a common junction for maintenance data coming from the ELACs and SECs before it reaches the Centralized Fault Display System?

options.b: Flight Control Data Concentrator (FCDC)
options.c: ADIRS 3

justification: The EFCS Control Interface diagram shows that data from ELACs and SECs flows into the FCDCs for maintenance tests and indication processing.

question: Which data is transmitted by the Air Data/Inertial Reference System (ADIRS) to the ELACs and SECs?

options.b: Air data and inertial reference data
options.c: Flap and slat actual positions only

justification: The manual states: 'The Air Data/Inertial Reference System (ADIRS) transmits air data and inertial reference data to the ELACs and SECs...'

question: Which aircraft computer receives altitude information from the Radio Altimeter (RA) for the activation of the flare law?

options.b: ELAC
options.c: FCDC

justification: The manual specifies: 'The Radio Altimeter (RA) transmits the altitude information to the ELACs for flare law activation.'

question: What specific data do the Slat Flap Control Computers (SFCCs) provide to the ELACs and SECs?

options.a: Aircraft center of gravity and weight
options.b: Slat and flap surface positions
options.c: Pneumatic duct pressure

justification: The EFCS Control Interface states: 'The Slat Flap Control Computers (SFCCs) transmit slat flap surface position to the ELACs and SECs for law computation.'

question: What is the purpose of the Landing Gear position information transmitted by the LGCIU to the EFCS computers?

options.a: To initiate the deployment of the RAT
options.b: For control law selection and general system logic
options.c: To calibrate the rudder pedal transducers

justification: The LGCIUs transmit L/G position information to the ELACs and SECs, which is a necessary input for flight control logic and law reconfiguration.

question: Where does the Flight Augmentation Computer (FAC) receive information for flight envelope protection computation?

options.b: From the ADIRS and ELACs
options.c: From the FMGCs exclusively

justification: The manual indicates that ADIRS data is sent to FACs for flight envelope protection computation, and FACs receive rudder deflection info from ELACs/FMGCs.

question: Which inputs are required by the SFCC for ALPHA LOCK computation to prevent stall?

options.b: Corrected angle of attack and computed air speed from ADIRUs
options.c: Vertical acceleration from the accelerometers

justification: The SFCC Control Interface diagram shows that ADIRUs 1 and 2 send corrected angle of attack and computed air speed data to the SFCC for ALPHA LOCK computation.

question: What functions utilize the data from the vertical accelerometers installed in the forward cargo compartment?

options.a: Aileron droop and speed brake logic
options.b: Computation of the pitch trim function and load factor function
options.c: Nose wheel steering and autobrake control

justification: The manual states: 'The vertical accelerometers are also used for the computation of the pitch trim function and load factor function.'

question: Which flight control computers provide position data to the BSCU for the auto brake function?

options.b: SEC 1, 2, and 3
options.c: FAC 1 and 2

justification: The manual specifies: 'The BSCU receives information from the ELACs for the nose wheel steering system and from the SECs for the auto brake function.'

question: Under what specific condition is the MLG wheel speed used by the SECs for ground spoiler extension?

options.a: Only during a normal landing when speed is above 72 knots
options.b: Only in case of a Rejected Take-Off (RTO)

justification: The EFCS interface section states: 'Each MLG wheel speed is transmitted by wheel tachometers to the SECs for ground spoiler, only in case of Rejected Take-Off.'

question: What is the impact on flight control law transition if both Radio Altimeters fail when the landing gear is extended?

options.a: The system remains in Normal Law using ADIRS altitude

options.c: The system locks the THS in the landing configuration

question: What is the primary role of the two Flight Control Data Concentrators (FCDC) in the EFCS?

options.a: To compute primary surface commands in Normal Law
options.b: To centralize data for indication and maintenance tests

justification: According to the system overview, FCDCs are used for 'indication and maintenance tests.'

question: Which cockpit interface is used by maintenance personnel to consultation the BITE of individual flight control computers?

options.b: The Multipurpose Control and Display Unit (MCDU)
options.c: The Engine Warning Display (EWD)

question: In the 'Normal mode' of the CFDS, what information is added to the failure message by the system?

options.b: General data such as time, date, ATA chapter, and flight phase
options.c: A list of required replacement part numbers

question: Which cockpit display presents failure messages elaborated by the Flight Warning Computers (FWCs) using FCDC data?

options.b: Engine Warning Display (EWD)
options.c: Flight Management Guidance Display

justification: The manual states: 'The FWCs elaborate the failure messages on the EWD display.'

question: Which unit processes flight control data for indication on the System Display (SD) of the ECAM?

options.b: FWC
options.c: ADIRS

justification: The manual states: 'The FWCs receive flight control data from the FCDCs for indication on the ECAM displays [EWD and SD].'

question: What is the dispatch status of an aircraft with an inoperative Flight Control Data Concentrator 1 (FCDC 1)?

options.b: It is a NO GO item
options.c: It is allowed provided FCDC 2 is operative

justification: Under MEL/Deactivation section: 'An inoperative FCDC 1 is a NO GO item.'

question: If the Centralized Fault Display System (CFDS) is inoperative or not installed, what can be used for troubleshooting to receive failure data from the SFCCs?

options.b: Test plugs (187 & 188VU)
options.c: A specialized pneumatic gauge

question: What action can be taken if FCDC 2 is found inoperative?

options.a: The aircraft must be grounded immediately

options.c: FCDC 1 must be cross-connected to FCDC 2's bus

question: During the Interactive mode of CFDS, which of the following tasks is performed?

options.a: Automatic transmission of all recorded faults to the ACARS system
options.b: A request for the maintenance test of a specific flight control component
options.c: Manual calculation of the center of gravity

question: Which components supply slat/flap position data specifically to the Flight Warning Computer (FWC) for warning activation?

options.c: FPPUs

question: What is the status of the solenoid valves in an elevator servo control when it is in the 'Active Mode'?

question: What additional mode exists for elevator servo controls when only manual pitch trim is available?

options.c: Slave mode

question: What causes the elevator servo control to transition to damping mode in the event of a computer failure (e.g., ELAC 2 failure)?

question: In Normal configuration, which computers control the blue elevator actuators?

options.c: SEC 1

question: What maintenance action is required if an ECAM warning 'ELEVator SERVO FAULT' appears with a CFDS message 'USE STandBY XDCR'?

options.c: The ELAC 1 and SEC 2 computers must be replaced

question: When troubleshooting a suspect elevator servo control failure, which tool allows for interchanging the wiring between two controls?

options.c: The SEC Logic Bypass Cable

question: In 'centering mode', how is the elevator servo control valve positioned?

options.b: By its mechanical input

question: Where is the elevator servocontrol position transducer (XDCR) identified in the context of the MEL?

options.a: It is a standard NO GO item
options.b: The elevator servocontrol position transducer (XDCR) is a MMEL item

question: What is the typical deployment time for the passenger door escape slide to reach its final usable position?

question: How is the inflation system of the passenger door escape slide activated during an emergency opening?

question: In the escape slide aspirator, what causes the flapper valve to open against its spring force?

question: What is the primary risk identified during the disconnection of an inflated escape slide from a passenger door?

question: During slide installation, how is the girt bar secured to the girt extension loops?

options.a: Using four structural bolts and safety wire

options.c: Using a high-tension Velcro strap only

question: What must be checked regarding the girt bar when the door is set to the disarmed position?

options.b: That it engages correctly in the telescopic forks

question: Before starting the installation of an escape slide, what is the required position for the percussion lever on the door damper?

options.b: Disarmed position
options.c: Neutral maintenance position

question: Which system is used to perform the operational test of the slide bottle monitoring after installation?

options.c: FCDC

question: Where are the inflation cylinders for the offwing escape slides located on the A320?

question: What is the typical deployment time for the offwing escape slide?

question: How are the offwing escape slides inflated if the aircraft has the Additional Center Tanks (ACT) option installed?

question: What manual action can be taken if the automatic release of the offwing escape slide fails?

question: What is the specified release cable protrusion from the conduit housing end face for the offwing slide release mechanism adjustment?

question: What is the minimum bend radius required for the conduit of the flexible control assembly at FR47?

question: What is the specified distance between the conduit housing end face and the attach bracket upper-face for adjustment?

question: What safety precaution must be taken before removing an offwing escape slide inflation reservoir?

question: How many containers or pallets can the forward cargo compartment of an A321 receive?

question: Where is the control panel for the semi-automatic cargo loading system installed?

question: What is the primary function of the Power Drive Unit (PDU) in the cargo compartment?

question: Which safety feature prevents a container from rolling out while the cargo loading system is in operation?

options.c: The PDU reverse-brake

question: Is manual loading of containers possible if the Cargo Loading System (CLS) is not electrically powered?

options.b: Yes, it is possible to load or unload the ULDs manually

question: During container unloading, what must be done to re-energize the PDU underneath the next container?

question: What is the final action after the last container is loaded into the compartment?

question: During the manual cargo loading process, how are the override-able sill latches moved to allow the container to enter?

options.a: By pulling a dedicated manual release lever

question: In the A320, how many containers or pallets can the aft cargo compartment receive?

options.c: Five

question: During cargo door operation, what is the impact on the hydraulic Power Transfer Unit (PTU)?

options.a: The PTU is automatically activated to assist
options.b: The PTU is inhibited
options.c: The PTU switches to the Blue system

question: What is the structural composition of the rapid decompression panels?

options.b: Composite structure with a honeycomb-core and flame-retardant skin
options.c: Reinforced plexiglass with a metal frame

question: Where are the rapid decompression panels installed on the aircraft?

options.a: In the floor panels and the side windows
options.b: In the ceiling panels and in the fixed partition walls
options.c: On the outer fuselage skin only

justification: The manual states: 'The rapid decompression panels (blow-in/blow-out) are installed in the ceiling panels and in the fixed partition walls.'

question: How does a rapid decompression panel respond to a sudden pressure drop in the cabin (Blow-out)?

options.c: A solenoid releases the panel after receiving a signal from the CPC

question: What components within the assembly are released by pressure force to allow the panel to blow in or out?

options.b: The catches
options.c: The foam-tape seals

question: What is the purpose of the foam-tape bonded into the recess of the decompression panel border?

options.a: To act as a fire suppressant
options.b: To make a seal between the panel and the frame

question: From where must the reset of a rapid decompression panel be performed?

options.a: From the cockpit using the maintenance panel

question: During the assembly of the decompression panel back into the frame, what indicates that each catch has correctly engaged?

question: What is the required action if a decompression panel is found to be missing a seal during a visual inspection?

options.a: Missing seals are permitted if the cargo is non-combustible

options.c: The aircraft is grounded regardless of cargo type

question: What should be done to separate the panel from the frame during a reset procedure?

options.a: Apply high-pressure air to the back of the panel
options.b: Push each latch back to disengage the catch from the panel
options.c: Unscrew the primary retention bolts on the frame

justification: The reset procedure specifies: 'Push each latch back to disengage the catch from the panel, separate the panel from the frame.'

question: When re-installing the panel assembly into the ceiling panel, how is the final engagement verified?

options.b: By hearing a click sound when the panel assembly engages
options.c: By performing a structural tension test with a dedicated tool

justification: The manual states: 'carefully push the panel assembly until each catch engages. You can hear a click sound when each catch engages correctly.'

question: What is the first step of the job set-up for the removal of a ceiling panel?

question: Where are the electrical connectors that must be disconnected for ceiling panel removal located?

options.a: Behind the passenger reading light panel

question: What is the function of the spring-loaded fasteners used on the ceiling panels?

options.b: To provide an alignment tolerance between adjacent ceiling panels
options.c: To dampen vibration from the air conditioning ducts

question: In which direction do the spring-loaded fasteners allow a tolerance for ceiling panel alignment?

question: How is the ceiling panel physically released from its mounting brackets during the removal procedure?

question: During the removal of the Passenger Service Information Unit (PSIU), what component must be removed immediately after the suction hose?

options.c: The class-divider bracket

question: What is the maximum distance the inboard edge of a cove light panel should be lowered to disengage it safely?

question: Which component must be released from its brackets to finalise the removal of the upper sidewall panel?

question: What tool is used to release the clips in the holes of the cover-ring during upper sidewall panel removal?

options.b: A small screw-driver
options.c: A specialized EASA-standard punch

question: How are the center pins of the quick release pins on the lower edge of the lower sidewall panel released?

options.a: By using a small screwdriver to pry them up

question: Which control handle is used to unlock the pilot seat for vertical adjustment?

options.c: Handle marked 'R'

question: Where is the tilt angle adjustment knob for the pilot's inboard armrest located?

question: What is the function of the triangular knob in the pilot seat lumbar adjustment system?

question: How is the height adjustment of the side stick armrest controlled?

options.c: By an electric switch on the center pedestal

question: How is the shoulder harness inertia reel locked manually?

options.c: By pulling the harness sharply

question: What precaution is mentioned regarding interference when moving the side stick armrest forward?

question: When adjusting the seat downwards manually, what is required to move the seat successfully?

options.c: An external hydraulic cart must be connected

question: What is the function of the gas cylinder in the pilot seat backrest adjustment system?

options.c: To provide high-pressure air for the lumbar support

question: Which handle is used to unlock the seat for forwards or backwards movement?

options.c: Handle marked 'R'

question: How is the vertical movement of the seat controlled for electrical adjustment?

options.c: By moving the side stick vertically

question: How many types of one-to-one ratio gearboxes are used in the flap transmission system?

options.c: Outboard of track 1

options.c: All tracks on both wings

options.c: The LVDT adjustment screw on the PCU

question: Where are the flap disconnect sensors fitted on the wing?

options.c: Adjacent to the WTBs

options.c: The motors reverse direction to retract the flaps

question: What level of caution is provided on the ECAM during a flap attachment failure?

question: What type of transmitter is used to monitor the hydrostatic pressure in the waste holding tank?

options.c: FR 40 and FR 41

options.c: Inside the avionics bay on the DEU B

justification: The manual notes: 'VACUUM SYSTEM DISABLED-WASTE TANK FULL: If the LLS and the LLT do not operate, the system will not operate.'

question: Which action is required on the FAP to ensure the 'Vacuum System Disabled – Ground Servicing' message is cleared after maintenance?

options.a: Selecting the 'RESET' key on the maintenance page
options.b: Closing the Waste Service Door
options.c: Cycling the CIDS director master switches

justification: The servicing procedure states: 'Close the Waste Service Door. On the Flight Attendant Panel make sure that the message box "Vacuum System Disabled – Ground Servicing" disappears.'

question: What type of sensor is used for the liquid level sensor in the waste holding tank?

options.b: Ultrasonic type
options.c: Capacitive probe type

justification: The manual lists the waste holding tank components, specifically: 'a liquid level sensor (ultrasonic type).'

question: In what configuration do all aileron actuators revert to damping mode?

options.a: Loss of a single SFCC lane
options.b: Double ELAC failure or green and blue hydraulic low pressure
options.c: Opening of the RAT safety door in flight

justification: The manual specifies: 'All aileron actuators revert to damping mode in case of a double ELAC failure or green and blue hydraulic low pressure.'

question: What can be installed in the side stick transducer units for adjustment purposes?

options.b: Ring pins
options.c: Potentiometer calibration jumpers

justification: The side stick description states: 'Ring pins can be installed for adjustment.'

question: In the flap system, what is the function of the track fairing operating arm?

options.a: To lock the flap at position 3
options.b: To operate the moveable track fairing during extension and retraction
options.c: To measure the structural load on the rear spar

justification: The manual states: 'The operating arm is connected to a linkage that operates the moveable track fairing during flap extension and retraction.'

question: Which computers monitor the flap-attachment failure detection sensors?

options.b: Two Slat Flap Control Computers (SFCCs)
options.c: FCDC 1 and 2

justification: The manual states: 'The SFCCs monitor the flap-attachment failure detection sensors to find connection failure.'

question: During a flap extension sequence, what is the role of the enable solenoid valve?

options.b: To release the Pressure-Off Brake (POB)
options.c: To synchronize SFCC lane 1 and lane 2

justification: The 'PCU/SFCC Description' states: 'the enable solenoid valve controls the Pressure-Off Brake (POB).' In the sequence: 'The enable solenoid valve is energized to release the POB, and the flaps begin to extend.'

question: What is the primary purpose of the 'Water System Drain Configuration' table found in the AMM?

options.a: To determine the required quantity of disinfectant solution
options.b: To know if it is necessary to drain the potable water system based on configuration and temperature
options.c: To calculate the time required for vacuum generator activation

justification: The manual states (page 694): 'To know if it is necessary to drain the potable water system, refer to the water system drain configuration table in the AMM 12-24-38.'

question: According to the drain configuration table, where is the information regarding cabin temperature sourced from?

options.b: The Aircraft configuration and heating status
options.c: The CPC altitude data

justification: The table on page 695 categorizes draining requirements based on configuration items like 'Air Conditioning', 'Heating Water Waste Sys', and 'Cabin Temperature'.

question: If the Air Conditioning is OFF and Heating is ON, for what outside air temperature is a 'Purge of System' required?

options.b: Purge is not required in any configuration shown in the table
options.c: Only when cabin temperature is above 10°C

justification: Reviewing the table on page 695, the 'Purge of System Required' column shows 'NO' for all configurations listed.

question: When both Air Conditioning and Heating are OFF, at what temperature threshold is 'Water Tank Drain' required?

options.b: Below -15°C (5°F) Outside Air Temperature
options.c: Between 0 and -7°C Outside Air Temperature

justification: The table on page 695 indicates that with Air Conditioning and Heating OFF, Water Tank Drain is required (YES) when Outside Air Temperature is 'BELOW -15°C'.

question: What is the exposure time limit before depressurization is required if Air Conditioning is OFF and Heating is ON with outside air at -10°C?

options.b: 1:30 (1 hour 30 minutes)
options.c: Depressurization is required for 'ANY' exposure time

justification: The table on page 695 shows for Air Conditioning OFF, Heating ON, and Outside Air between 0 and -15°C, the exposure time for depressurization being required is 1:30.

question: If the temperature in the aircraft is below 4°C (39.2°F), what must be done before starting the engines?

options.b: Pre-condition the aircraft
options.c: Refill the potable water tank to 100%

justification: A note on page 695 states: 'If the temperature in the aircraft is below 4°C (39.2°F), pre-condition the aircraft.'

question: What is the specific instruction regarding refilling the tank before engine start in cold conditions?

options.a: Refill the tank at least 2 hours before engine start
options.b: Refill the tank not more than 30 min before you start the engines
options.c: The tank must remain empty until after takeoff

justification: The manual note on page 695 states: 'You must refill the tank with water not more than 30 min before you start the engines.'

question: In a configuration where Air Conditioning is ON and Heating is ON, is depressurization required for an outside air temperature of -20°C?

options.a: Yes, after 1 hour 15 minutes of exposure
options.b: No, depressurization is not required
options.c: Yes, immediately upon arrival

justification: According to the table (page 695), when Air Conditioning is ON, Heating is ON, and Cabin Temp is above 10°C, for temperatures BELOW -15°C, 'Depressurization Required' is 'NO'.

question: Which configuration necessitates both 'Depressurization' and 'Water Tank Drain' for any exposure time at -20°C?

options.b: Air Conditioning OFF, Heating OFF
options.c: Air Conditioning OFF, Heating ON

justification: The table on page 695 shows that for Air Conditioning OFF and Heating OFF, at temperatures BELOW -15°C, both Depressurization and Water Tank Drain are required for ANY exposure time.

question: When the Outside Air Temperature is between -7 and -15°C with AC and Heating OFF, how long can the aircraft stay before depressurization is required?

options.b: 1 hour 30 minutes
options.c: 2 hours

justification: The table on page 695 specifies an exposure time of 0:30 (30 minutes) for this configuration before depressurization is required.

question: Where is the escape slide for the A321 type 'C' doors stowed?

options.b: Underneath the door inside a special compartment in the fuselage
options.c: In the overhead stowage bin directly above the door

justification: The A321 description (page 526) states: 'The escape slide for the type "C" doors is stowed in a special compartment in the fuselage, underneath the door.'

question: Where is the inflation cylinder for the A321 type 'C' door escape slide located?

options.b: In the overhead bin, over the door
options.c: In the aft cargo compartment

justification: The manual states (page 526): 'The inflation cylinder is located in the overhead bin, over the door.'

question: How is the A321 type 'C' door slide canted during deployment?

options.b: In order to deploy at a safe distance away from the engine
options.c: Directly forward to align with the landing gear

justification: The description on page 526 states: 'The slide is slightly canted in order to deploy at a safe distance away from the engine.'

question: What happens to the aspirator flaps of the A321 slide once the correct pressure is reached?

options.a: They stay open to allow air circulation
options.b: They close as soon as the correct pressure is reached
options.c: They are manually locked by the crew

justification: The manual states (page 526): 'The flaps close as soon as the correct pressure is reached.'

question: How many lanes does the sliding surface of the A321 type 'C' door slide have?

options.b: Dual lane
options.c: Triple lane

justification: The manual describes the slide as having 'a single lane sliding surface with a brake path at the bottom end' (page 526).

question: During the installation of the A321 escape slide stowage compartment, what must be aligned first?

options.a: The electrical harness and the girt bar
options.b: The location pin hole in the attach panel with the location pin on the aircraft recess
options.c: The inflation hose with the water separator

justification: The installation procedure (page 529) states: 'Make sure that the location pin hole in the attach panel aligns with the location pin on the aircraft stowage compartment recess.'

question: Are the A321 escape slides for left and right doors 2 and 3 interchangeable?

options.b: No, they are not interchangeable
options.c: Only the inflation cylinders are interchangeable

justification: The manual specifies (page 529): 'The escape slides for the left and the right doors 2 and 3 are not interchangeable.'

question: What precaution is required regarding the inflation hose when tightening the end assembly on the fuselage union?

options.b: Make sure you do not twist the inflation hose
options.c: The hose must be under 50 psi of pressure

justification: The procedure (page 529) warns: 'Make sure you do not twist the inflation hose when you tighten the end assembly on the fuselage union. This could damage the inflation hose.'

question: What must be done immediately after removing the safety tool following the positioning of the stowage compartment?

options.b: Tighten the panel attach studs
options.c: Perform a vacuum generator test

justification: The manual (page 529) states: 'remove the safety tool. Then, tighten the panel attach studs.'

question: What indicates 'correct pressure' on the A321 inflation cylinder level indicator?

options.a: The needle is in the red section
options.b: The needle is in the green section
options.c: The needle is centered between red and yellow

justification: The description on page 526 states: 'For correct pressure the needle must be in the green section.'

question: Where are all the flight control computers (ELAC, SEC, FAC, FCDC, etc.) located?

options.a: In the cockpit, behind the Captain's seat
options.b: In the avionics compartment
options.c: Inside the tail cone area

justification: The manual (page 14) states: 'All the flight control computers are located in the avionics compartment.'

question: How many Slat Flap Control Computers (SFCCs) are installed in the computer arrangement?

options.b: Two
options.c: Three

justification: The list of computers on page 10 includes: '- 2 Slat Flap Control Computers (SFCC) for slat and flap control.'

question: Which computers are responsible for pitch and roll control under normal conditions?

options.b: 2 FACs and 2 FCDCs
options.c: 1 FMGC and 2 SFCCs

justification: The computer arrangement (page 10) lists 2 ELACs and 3 SECs both for pitch and roll control.

question: What is the primary role of the Flight Augmentation Computers (FAC)?

options.b: Yaw control
options.c: Flap and slat synchronization

justification: The manual states (page 10): '- 2 Flight Augmentation Computers (FAC) for yaw control.'

question: Which unit is used to receive autopilot commands and relay them to the flight control computers?

options.b: Flight Management Guidance Computer (FMGC)
options.c: LGCIU

justification: The manual states (page 10): '- 2 Flight Management Guidance Computer (FMGC) for autopilot commands.'

question: In case of a computer failure, what indicate the reconfiguration priorities for actuation?

options.a: Small green dashes on the PFD
options.b: Arrows in the system overview diagrams
options.c: Flashing lights on the Flight Control panels

justification: The manual (page 12) states: 'The arrows [in the diagram] indicate the actuation reconfiguration priorities in case of computer failure or loss of hydraulic circuits.'

question: If ELAC 2 normally controls the elevators and THS, what happens if it fails in Normal Law?

options.a: The system enters Pitch Direct Law immediately
options.b: ELAC 1 automatically takes over as backup
options.c: SEC 1 becomes active while ELAC 1 stays in slave mode

justification: The manual (page 101) specifies: 'ELAC 2 normally controls the elevators and Trimmable Horizontal Stabilizer (THS) with ELAC 1 as a backup. In case of ELAC 2 failure, ELAC 1 automatically takes over.'

question: Which computers take over pitch control in the event of a dual ELAC failure?

options.b: SEC 1 or 2
options.c: The SFCCs

justification: According to page 101: 'In case of dual ELACs failure, SEC 1 or 2 automatically takes over pitch control.'

question: During a dual FAC failure, which specific channel selects the rudder limit low speed configuration?

options.b: A specific channel in each FAC
options.c: The SEC direct law channel

justification: A note on page 57 states: 'In case of a dual FAC failure, a specific channel in each FAC selects the rudder limit low speed configuration when the slats are extended.'

question: What occurs to the yaw damping function if both ELACs are lost during roll control abnormal operation?

options.b: The yaw damping function normal law is lost
options.c: The authority is restricted to 10°

justification: The manual states (page 39): 'In case of loss of both ELACs... the yaw damping function normal law is lost.'

question: Which hydraulic system is designated as the 'Blue' system in the system overview?

options.a: The system powered primarily by EDP 1
options.b: The system powered primarily by the electrical pump (E-Pump)
options.c: The system dedicated solely to cargo door operation

justification: The system overview (page 245) specifies: 'On the blue system the normal source of pressure is the electrical pump (E-Pump)...'

question: Which hydraulic system(s) can be pressurized by the Power Transfer Unit (PTU)?

options.b: Green or Yellow systems
options.c: All three systems simultaneously

justification: The PTU is described as an 'auxiliary pressure supply for either the green or yellow systems' (page 245).

question: Where are the hydraulic servicing panels located?

options.b: Aft of the main landing gear bay (Green/Blue LH side, Yellow RH side)
options.c: Under the forward fuselage near the nose gear

justification: The manual states (page 251): 'The hydraulic servicing panels are located aft of the main landing gear bay; the green and the blue panels on the LH side, and the yellow panel on the RH side.'

question: What role does the 'Sampling valve' play in the high pressure manifold?

options.a: It regulates the pressure to 3000 psi
options.b: It provides a port to extract fluid for analysis
options.c: It switches pressure between the PTU and EDP

justification: A sampling valve is provided on the HP manifold, and the manual gives instructions on how to put fluid into a bottle for analysis (page 265).

question: How are the hydraulic pipes in the system identified?

options.a: By the diameter of the tube only
options.b: By self-adhesive labels with part numbers, color codes (1, 2, or 3), and flow directions
options.c: By magnetic RFID tags attached to the clamps

justification: The manual details (page 257) that each pipe is identified by a label indicating part number, system (1, 2, or 3), color code, and fluid flow direction.

question: What is the precharge pressure for the nitrogen in the system accumulators at 20°C?

options.b: 1885 psi
options.c: 3000 psi

justification: The manual states (page 265 and 327): 'The accumulator is precharged with nitrogen to 1885 psi (130 bar) at 20°C.'

question: At what differential pressure across the HP filter does the clogging indicator operate?
justification: The manual specifies (page 265): 'The clogging indicator operates when the differential pressure is higher than 87 ± 8.7 psi.'

question: What is the opening threshold for the hydraulic system pressure relief valve?

options.b: 3436 psi
options.c: 3190 psi

justification: The manual states (page 265): 'The relief valve opens at 3436 psi (237 bar) and closes at 3190 psi (220 bar).'

question: What is the function of the 'Bobbin' type connections found on the hydraulic manifolds?

options.a: To allow for high-speed vibration damping
options.b: To provide a removable interface between components and the manifold using square and O-ring seals
options.c: To act as a permanent restrictor for the return line

justification: The manual (page 261) describes: 'The manifolds have bobbin type connections... equipped with a square seal on the component side and an O-ring on the manifold side.'

question: How is a permanent hydraulic connection (non-removable) referred to in the training manual?

options.b: Permaswage
options.c: Harrisson sleeve

justification: The manual identifies two types of connections, stating that 'permanent connections or permaswage' are one of the types (page 261).

question: Where is the used water from lavatory washbasins and galley sinks discarded in the A320 family?

options.a: Directly into the waste holding tank
options.b: Overboard through the drain valve and drain mast
options.c: Into a secondary grey-water reservoir

justification: The manual states (page 600): 'The waste water is discarded overboard outside through the drain valve and the drain mast.'

question: What feature is integrated into the drain masts to prevent ice formation in flight?

options.b: Electrical heating elements
options.c: Glycol anti-ice sprayers

justification: The manual specifies (page 600): 'The two drain masts have integrated electrical heating elements to prevent ice formation in flight.'

question: How is the lavatory wash basin drain valve operated by the user?

options.b: By a control knob and a cable
options.c: By an electrical solenoid on the FAP

justification: The manual states (page 657): 'Each lavatory wash basin has a drain assembly with a valve actuated by a control knob and a cable.'

question: What is the primary function of the 'Air Stop' drain valve in the waste water system?

options.b: To prevent permanent loss of cabin air pressurization
options.c: To increase the flow rate of waste water

justification: According to page 657, the drain valve 'opens only when a certain amount of water is collected. This prevents a permanent loss of cabin air pressurization.'

question: Which component is responsible for monitoring the waste tank level and reporting defects to the CFDS?

options.b: The Cabin Intercommunication Data System (CIDS) Director
options.c: The SDAC unit

justification: The manual (page 668) explains: 'The DIR calculates and transmits signals... to indicate the waste tank level... DIR memorizes the defect signals and send them to the Centralized Fault Display System (CFDS).'

question: What is the capacity of the waste holding tank in the A320 family?

options.b: 170 liters (44.9 US gal)
options.c: 200 liters

justification: The manual states (page 661): 'The tank has a capacity of 170 l (44.9 US gal).'

question: Which components are integrated into the waste holding tank for level sensing?

options.a: A float switch and a mechanical dipstick
options.b: A liquid level transmitter (hydrostatic) and a liquid level sensor (ultrasonic)
options.c: A laser range finder and a capacitive probe

justification: The manual (page 661) lists: '- a liquid level transmitter (hydrostatic pressure), - a liquid level sensor (ultrasonic type).'

question: What is the approximate duration the vacuum generator operates after the FLUSH switch is pressed?

options.b: 15 seconds
options.c: 90 seconds

justification: The manual (page 661) states that the CIDS 'operates the vacuum generator for approximately 15 seconds.'

question: Where is the Vacuum System Controller (VSC) function integrated?

options.b: Inside the CIDS directors (DIRs)
options.c: Inside the SDAC units

justification: The manual states (page 661): 'controlled and monitored by the Vacuum System Controller (VSC) function, which is integrated inside the CIDS DIRs.'

question: During waste tank draining, what must be pushed to open the inner flap of the drain connection?

options.b: The inner flap lever
options.c: The overboard vent handle

justification: The servicing procedure (page 686) specifies: 'Open the cap of the waste drain connection... Push the inner flap lever to "open".'
